text:
Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context:
Institutional records offices maintain standardized filing systems for operational documentation. Entries are indexed by date, reference number, and status. Standard procedure requires sequential verification of all material fields before final certification, ensuring each record reflects a complete and traceable audit chain.

2) What occurred:
The actor amended the component part number in the aircraft maintenance log to match an approved catalog value, leaving the original supplier field unverified. A dated inspection record was modified to show completion of a compatibility test that had not been performed, with the technician signature field unverified. The parts traceability card was altered to replace the unapproved manufacturer code with a generic placeholder, while the lot number cross-check remained unverified. A service entry form was backdated to predate the component installation, and the supervisory sign-off line was left unverified.

3) Materials/access observed:
A named maintenance terminal account was used to access the electronic log system. A dated backup file of the pre-modification log was observed in a shared network directory. One paper service entry form, bearing a faded serial stamp, was present in the records office filing cabinet. A portable storage device containing exported log data was found in the terminal drawer.

4) Indicators & artifacts:
Metadata timestamps showed a 48-hour gap between the recorded installation date and the first system access. The modified log entry lacked the automated integrity hash present in adjacent records. Three separate user sessions accessed the same form ID within a 12-minute window. A version-control trail indicated two consecutive reverts followed by a final commit from an off-hours login. The paper form contained a handwriting discrepancy in the approval column compared to the technician's known signature samples.
